researcher_notes: Covered all 5 assigned vendors: QSR Automations (ConnectSmart KDS), Fresh KDS, Delaget, Meazure Up, Jolt. Corporate-structure churn was unusually heavy in this batch -- 4 of the 5 vendors have changed hands or been absorbed into a larger platform since roughly 2023-2025, and in each case the vendor's own historical case-study/press-release URLs (qsrautomations.com, delaget.com, meazureup.com) now 301/302-redirect into the acquirer's site, so most citations below had to be recovered via search-index snippets/cache rather than a live fetch of the original page -- flagged per-record where that applies. Only Fresh KDS remains an independent private company as far as I can confirm. The franchisee-vs-brand distinction called out in the task instructions mattered most for Delaget (both of its two deepest relationships -- MAS Restaurant Group and Diversified Restaurant Group -- are individual Taco Bell franchisee operators, not a Taco Bell corporate deal) and came up again for Jolt (Buffalo Wild Wings evidence is a single multi-location franchisee, not the brand) and Fresh KDS (Smashburger evidence is specifically the UK master-franchisee operation). MeazureUp was the deepest/richest vendor in this batch (10 records, several with named-executive on-record quotes in QSR Magazine sponsored content -- Krystal, Golden Corral, Osmow's Shawarma, Pizza Ranch). QSR Automations was second-deepest (5 records) despite the fact that, per the June 2025 Crunchtime merger, its products are now literally being renamed Crunchtime Kitchen/Crunchtime Host -- meaning fresh QSR Automations-branded evidence going forward should probably be captured under the (out-of-scope-for-this-batch) Crunchtime vendor line instead. Also corrected two apparent mis-tagged rows in the existing restaurant_tech_research_2026-07-21.json candidate_evidence array: a 'Pizza Ranch' row filed under Delaget was actually a Taco Bell/DRG case study (keyword collision on the word 'ranch'); a 'Daily Grill' row filed under Delaget was actually referencing the DailyPay payroll vendor mentioned on the same page (keyword collision on 'Daily'). Pizza Ranch turned out to be a genuine, correctly-sourced MeazureUp customer instead, found independently.

vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: QSR Automations -- received a majority growth investment from Battery Ventures (announced 2024-11-01), then merged with Crunchtime (announced/completed mid-2025, per restauranttechnologynews.com 2025-06-11 and Crunchtime's own blog). Its flagship products, ConnectSmart Kitchen and ConnectSmart Host, have been formally renamed Crunchtime Kitchen and Crunchtime Host as of that merger. QSR Automations is not shut down -- it continues operating as 'QSR Automations by Crunchtime' -- but it is no longer an independent company, and any post-mid-2025 evidence for this product line probably belongs under the existing Crunchtime vendor entity (out of scope for this batch per the task instructions) rather than a standalone QSR Automations line going forward.

Delaget -- acquired by PAR Technology Corporation (NYSE American: PAR) for $132M, deal announced 2025-01-02 (closed 2024-12-31). Delaget's product has been rebranded 'PAR OPS' (with 'Coach' and 'Coach AI' as sub-product names), and delaget.com now 301-redirects into partech.com/delaget/, a PAR-branded landing page. Not defunct, but no longer independent -- future evidence will likely surface under a 'PAR OPS' or 'PAR Technology' name rather than 'Delaget.'

Meazure Up -- combined in 2025-03-04 with ComplianceMate and Storewise under a newly launched parent brand, 'Ladle' (backed by Nexa Equity, per Software Equity Group and PrivSource deal coverage). meazureup.com press-release URLs now 301-redirect into ladle.com/resources/. MeazureUp is not shut down as a product line (Ladle's own site still markets it as 'MeazureUp' under the Ladle umbrella), but it is no longer an independently branded company -- future evidence will likely surface under 'Ladle' rather than 'MeazureUp' alone.

Jolt -- acquired by Digi International Inc. (NASDAQ: DGII) for approximately $145.5M, deal completed 2025-08-18, being integrated into Digi's SmartSense business unit. Unlike the other three, Jolt's own branding/product name does not appear to be changing (jolt.com continues operating under the Jolt name) -- flagged here as a corporate-ownership change rather than a rename, but worth tracking in case Digi folds the Jolt brand into SmartSense branding later.
